messages:
maria: FYI, last night we had two OOMs on prod-serve-3 during long-context chat loads (seq ~12k). looks tied to the cache-shard drain path after the kernel selection change. attaching quick notes below.
adeep: Ugh. Is this the patch that biases kernel picker toward fused-gemm?
jordan: yes — that change reduced GPU cycles but I suspected it might change peak alloc pattern. any stack traces or logs?
maria: paste from node logs: `oom: alloc failed while compacting kv-shard(23) size=1.2GB target_free=128MB`. Also saw repeated page faults coming from `kv_evict_worker` spikes.
lee: can you dump slabmap and the eviction watermark at time of crash?
maria: slabmap at 2024-06-09T02:12Z: "total_slab=14.7GB used=14.1GB free=600MB fragmentation=11%"; eviction_watermark=0.95 (we were at 0.98 when crash happened).
olivia: 0.98 is scary. Was the reuse accounting per-shard or global?
maria: per-shard. the shard in question had a sudden reuse counter reset (we think) so it didn't consider some hot prefixes reusable and tried to allocate new pages instead of reclaiming.
adeep: that smells like a race in the reuse refcount bump on page insert. we recently moved reuse bump into the kernel hotpath to avoid extra copies.
jordan: repro steps I ran locally: `curl -H "X-Sequence-Length: 12000" -X POST https://host/api/stream -d @long_prompt.json --concurrency 8` hits the issue within ~3-5k tokens. I attached a tiny flamegraph snippet: ```flamegraph
kv_insert() 48%
kv_evict_worker 22%
gpu_kernel_launch 15%
other 15%
```
lee: interesting that kv_insert dominates. that explains why fused-gemm change impacted memory pattern: fused path keeps more transient buffers live which nudges eviction timing.
maria: quick mitigation I rolled out at 02:25: set runtime flag `kv_drain_slack=0.12` and lowered eviction_watermark from 0.95 -> 0.88 on that pool. no OOMs since (2.5h).
olivia: good quick fix. longer term we should: 1) ensure reuse bump is atomic across shards 2) add a conservative pre-evict that looks ahead for transient kernel allocations 3) expose per-model fallback to smaller kv representation.
adeep: agree. I can prototype atomic bump (compare-and-swap on refcount) and a gated check for fused kernel path to trigger early eviction.
jordan: we should also add a small graceful-degrade that truncates oldest KV entries for streaming sessions > N tokens and returns a header `x-kv-truncated: true`. that will keep latency low and avoid full spill.
lee: telemetry ask: we need a histogram of post-insert resident set change by kernel type (fused vs unfused) + sequence-length bucket. add a counter for reuse-reset events.
maria: I've added a perf test in the nightly suite: `tests/longctx/kv_shard_drain_profile.py` which runs against a synthetic workload with increasing seq lengths and asserts no sess OOM at 16k.
olivia: any rollback required for the kernel pick change? customer impact?
maria: no customer-facing rollback yet — p50 latency increased from 52ms -> 68ms for some workloads with the drain_slack change, but SLA still met. cost slightly up for that pool (~6%).
adeep: plan: (1) patch reuse refcount atomic -> canary on staging today, (2) add lookahead pre-evict gated behind `kv_lookahead=1`, (3) implement truncation fallback and header, (4) add telemetry + alert for reuse-reset rate.
jordan: timeline OK. I can own (3) and tests. lee will own telemetry dashboard.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-618 - prod-serve-3 OOMs (linked to thread 1718005432).
deploy-bot: Can confirm runtime flag change deployed to pool prod-serve-3 at 2024-06-09T02:26Z by maria.
lee: assigning tasks: adeep -> reuse-cas, jordan -> truncation-fallback, olivia -> rollout plan for kernel-picker rollback if needed, maria -> longctx nightly test + postmortem notes. please add PRs to the 'kv-stability' epic.
maria: poking in to remind: include a small synthetic that toggles kernel picker to fused/unfused in CI so we don't regress again.
olivia: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
